summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is a highly technical computational physics research session (Session 38) in an ongoing multi-session project called the "Löwdin challenge" — an attempt to derive and validate the Madelung n+ℓ rule (which determines the order of electron subshell filling across the periodic table) from first principles using relativistic Hartree-Fock calculations. The person is directing Claude through a structured research protocol involving predictions before runs, gate verification, census checks, and careful attribution of physical mechanisms across 13 atomic rows (Sc, Y, La, Ce, Gd, Lu, Hf, Ac, Th, Pa, U, Cm, Rf).

The session's primary work was computing and evaluating LS term/multiplet energies as the first row-differential object measured on the Th/Ac pair — the residual problem the project has been narrowing toward. A key structural finding emerged: the neutral atom's term energy cancels exactly out of the ionization gap, so only the two ions' term energies matter. This algebra was then shown to generalize to spin-orbit (SO) corrections as well. The LS term correction resolved Th (the one previously wrong row) but broke four others (Hf, Pa, U, Cm), and SO was shown — via a sign prediction filed before computation — to push every row further in the same direction as the LS correction rather than quenching it, eliminating SO as a companion mechanism. The next candidate identified is a feasibility test on the F^k scale: whether a uniform reduction factor (motivated by correlation screening of multipole interactions in HF) can restore all 13 rows without fitting a constant.

The person communicates concisely and directs Claude's approach through brief rulings. A key ruling in this session was that the three design decisions for the term-energy run (source of ion ground arrangements, frozen vs. relaxed orbitals, whether to include SO) "can be determined by studying the other rows" rather than being chosen — meaning Claude was directed to derive conventions from the data structure rather than assert them. When Claude's explanation of the decisions was too technical, the person requested a plain restatement. The person also granted permission to extend the session beyond the initial handoff point when additional work was feasible. The project enforces strict protocols: predictions must be filed before any code is read or run, faults must be registered and not suppressed, fitted constants are forbidden, and "comparison decides" rather than assertion. A fault registered this session (F38.1) involved omitting `.json` data files from the runtime rebuild loop, caught at gate verification before any new results were read.

**The register's own summary and its new front matter disagreed by ten.** *The front matter counted entries matching a single-number label; the summary counted every label including grouped ones like "305, 361."* **Both now count the same list.** *Two counts of one thing, differing, is exactly what audit 22 CENSUS exists to catch — and it did not, because the register compendium is not the book.*

**Where the corrections came from, recorded as a taxonomy.** *Four kinds resolve the faults in this register: **a published result** — R∞ → R_M is Bohr 1913, made after Fowler objected the Pickering series did not fit; **a measurement the work already held** — the multiplicity constraint proved at 1139 and not carried into the operator until 1178; **an audit written after the fact** — the dependency cycle caught only when audit 24 existed; and **the person's correction** — pushing back where the assistant stopped looking too early.* **The fourth has no register number of its own and appears throughout.**

**AND THE WIDENED PATTERN EXPOSED A THIRD FAULT: EIGHT ENTRIES WITH UNPAIRED BOLD MARKERS.** *Each had a bold opened inside an italic block and never closed, so the marker leaked into the PDF as literal asterisks. ## 34. The Löwdin challenge

*In 1969 Per-Olov Löwdin set a challenge: derive the n+ℓ filling rule from the
Schrödinger equation. It has stood since. This chapter states the challenge, what
the method delivered, and how the method itself did the work.*

### The problem, and the wrong target

Löwdin asked for the n+ℓ rule. **The rule is not what atoms obey.**

Read from the observed ground configurations of all 108 neutrals, the sequence in
which subshells OPEN is

> 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p 6s **5d 4f** 6p 7s **6d 5f** 7p

**Madelung's rule inverts 5d/4f and 6d/5f.** Lanthanum opens 5d at Z = 57 and 4f
does not appear until cerium; actinium opens 6d at Z = 89 and 5f not until
protactinium. *Seventeen of nineteen openings agree; two do not.*

**So deriving n+ℓ exactly would mean deriving something false at two elements.**
The target is the ORDER, and n+ℓ is a name for it that is 89% accurate.

> **ν(n,ℓ,q) = n − a·√( n − ℓ − 1 + q/2(2ℓ+1) )**
>
> **The incoming electron occupies the subshell of least ν among those with
> q < 2(2ℓ+1).**

**Both Pauli quantities appear.** The capacity 2(2ℓ+1) governs admissibility AND
sits inside the radicand. *The radicand is the count of states below: complete
lower shells of the same ℓ, plus the fraction of the current one already filled.*

**And the occupancy enters only through Pauli.** With the fraction q/2(2ℓ+1) in the
radicand the scatter in a within a subshell falls from 0.187 to 0.041 at 3p, 0.119
to 0.028 at 4p, 0.088 to 0.018 at 5p, 0.059 to 0.021 at 6p, 0.086 to 0.047 at 5d.
**Raw occupancy makes every one worse.** *The law needs no new coordinate.

The 1969 Löwdin Challenge
In his 1969 paper ("Some Comments on the Periodic System of the Elements"), quantum chemist Per-Olov Löwdin posed what became known as the Löwdin Challenge.  
Rather than listing individual chemical elements (like Hydrogen or Gold), the challenge asks to derive the fundamental structural elements and rules governing the periodic table directly from first principles of quantum mechanics.
The exact elements that need to be derived from first principles are:
The Madelung (n + \ell) Rule (or Klechkovsky Rule): The primary objective of the challenge is to derive the rule that determines the order in which electronic shells are filled in neutral, multi-electron atoms (orbitals fill in order of increasing n + \ell, and for equal values of n + \ell, in order of increasing n).  
The Length/Sequence of Periodic Periods: Deriving the exact shell-capacity sequence that defines the length of successive periods in the periodic table: 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32...  
The Building-Up (Aufbau) Principle: Explaining the electronic ground state configurations across the periodic system strictly via the Schrödinger equation and electrostatic/quantum mechanical interactions, without relying on empirical parameters or semi-empirical models.

"""madelung.py -- do measured quantum defects organise on n+l?

Register 1249. Loewdin 1969 named the derivation of the n+l rule a major unsolved
problem. The closest thing to a derivation is Demkov & Ostrovsky, n+l filling rule
in the periodic system and focusing potentials, Sov. Phys. JETP 35 (1972) 66-69:
a potential class whose levels depend only on n+l.

The quantum defect is exactly the quantity measuring how a real atomic potential
departs from Coulomb. So the question has a MEASURABLE form:

    does the effective quantum number n* = n - delta(l) order by n+l ?

Concretely, the Madelung rule says a subshell with a smaller n+l fills first, and
"fills first" means "lies lower in energy". For a Rydberg channel,

    E = - Zc^2 R / (n - delta)^2

so lower energy means smaller n*. The rule therefore predicts

    (n+l) < (n'+l')  =>  n* < n*'          [MADELUNG ORDER]

and, for ties in n+l, smaller n first.

The Method 1.6 — The Index of Indices-1.md
*Janet recognised the (n+ℓ) rule before Madelung, who arrived at it around 1926 and did not publish until 1936.* The shell-length sequence 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32 follows from the rule by the Klechkovski–Hakala formulas.

**What only it contributes.** *That E is coordinate-relative, demonstrated on one subject rather than argued.* The periodic table and Janet index THE SAME 118 elements and give E = 36 and E = 0. **No pair of indexes anywhere else in this work makes that point as cleanly, because no other pair shares its subject exactly.**

**And an open problem sits underneath it.** *Why* the n+ℓ ordering holds is unresolved — Löwdin's challenge, still open; see Allen & Knight, *The Löwdin challenge: origin of the n+l, n (Madelung) rule*, Int. J. Quantum Chem. **90** (2003) 80–88. **This work uses the ordering and does not explain it**, and the orbital-collapse result (registers 1187–1190) is a measurement against Janet's boundaries, not a derivation of them.

## The nuclide chart — (Z, N)

**What it is.** The measured nuclides indexed by proton and neutron count, E = **9**.

**Where it comes from.** The chart is Segrè's, in use since the 1940s; the values are the AME2020 evaluation.

**What only it contributes.** *A defect whose cells are identifiable physics.* The nine cells are the mass formula's pairing and clustering terms. **It is the only index here where E > 0 and every missing cell can be named**, which is what makes the defect a measurement rather than a score.

## The calendar — (month, day)

**What it is.** 365 cells in a box of 372, E = **7**.

**Where it comes from.** The Gregorian reform of 1582, on the Julian arrangement of 46 BC. *The month lengths are a political inheritance, not a natural one.*

**What only it contributes.** *A subject with no physics in it at all.* The calendar shows the operator working on an object whose constraints are entirely conventional, **and 365 = 5 · 73 with E = 7 is the price of keeping January first.** No other index here separates the method from the physics so completely.

## The box ordering and the chessboard

**What they are.** ℓ ≥ w ≥ h over five values: 35 cells in 125, E = 0. And (rank, file): 64 cells in 64, E = 0.

**What only they contribute.** *The floor and the ceiling.* The chessboard is a full product — E = 0 because there is no constraint at all. ORDER = [(1,0),(2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1),(4,0),(3,2),(4,1),(5,0),(4,2),(5,1),(6,0),
         (4,3),(5,2),(6,1),(7,0),(5,3),(6,2),(7,1),(8,0)]
OPEN = {}; _z = 0
for _n, _l in ORDER: OPEN[(_n,_l)] = _z + 1; _z += 2*(2*_l+1)

def config(ne):
    """the aufbau ground configuration for ne electrons, as (n, l, occ)"""
    out = []; left = ne
    for n, l in ORDER:
        if left <= 0: break
        cap = 2*(2*l+1); k = min(cap, left)
        out.append((n, l, k)); left -= k
    return out

def core_p(ne, l):
    """how many orbitals of this l the core already holds"""
    return sum(1 for n, ll, o in config(ne) if ll == l and o > 0)

def delta(Z, c, l):
    ne = Z - c + 1
    p = core_p(ne - 1, l)
    t = math.log(c + 1) / c
    if p > 0:
        e = max(E0 + E1*math.log(max(ne, 2)), 0.05)
        return A * (p**e) * ne**K * t
    # p = 0: the collapse branch
    v = [n for n, ll, o in config(ne - 1) if ll == l and o > 0]
    n0 = (max(v) + 1) if v else l + 1
    thr = OPEN.get((n0, l), 999)
    C = min(max((Z - thr + 4.0)/8.0, 0.0), 1.0)
    return HH * C * ((ne - 1)/ne) * ne**K * t

def n0_of(ne, l):
    """the first Pauli-allowed n for this l -- p nodes forced by orthogonality"""
    return core_p(ne, l) + l + 1

def madelung_key(n, l):
    return (n + l, n)

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md

Files survive a container death; §H.0 states that what dies is WHY — which thread was open, which decision was M's and unmade, which number is a choice wearing the appearance of a measurement. So §H.1 requires four things to travel and calls three of four the dangerous case because it looks like a handoff: the work (the bank), the record (the register), the orientation (DIGEST.md), and the state (the bridge). §H.3 makes the TRANSCRIPTS travel into the work tree, on the ground that the register carries conclusions and only a transcript carries the reasoning and the discarded route. §H.4 forbids summarising anything that can be carried, and forbids rewriting history to match the present — which is why R 1656 left three stale cell counts standing inside historical statements. §H.6 sorts every figure into MEASURED, CHOSEN or INHERITED, because the second kind reads as the first and that is where damage comes from.** *AND §H.8 IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT A PROTOCOL RATHER THAN AN INTENTION. THREADS WERE DETECTED BY THE SAME EXPRESSION THAT REQUIRED AN OWNER, so the clause's stated failure mode — a thread with no owner — could not arise: such a thread does not fail the match, it fails to be a thread. §H.8 says each clause must be capable of failing and §4.6 requires that capability before a pass is evidence; C6 had the form of a check without its content. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ground.py -- the OBSERVED ground configurations, Z = 1 to 108.

NIST ASD ver. 5.12, GSIE interface, retrieved 2026-08-09:
    Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J., and NIST ASD Team (2024).
    NIST Atomic Spectra Database, DOI 10.18434/T4W30F.

Register 1306. Every previous version of this work built configurations by aufbau
and patched the exceptions by hand. That table was wrong at Pd -- aufbau plus my
patch gave [Kr]4d9 5s, and the observed configuration is [Kr]4d10 with no 5s at
all -- and at Lr, which is [Rn]5f14 7s2 7p and not 6d.

This file is READ, not computed. It is the ordering the Loewdin challenge asks
about, stated by measurement.
"""

The Method 1.6 — The Register-1.md
The Ritz refit must be run on the full capture set before any threshold downstream is trusted.* **That is a session's work and it is the right next one** — *because until it is done, every accuracy figure in the compendium is measured against a quantity that is not noise.*

### 1157

**THE SIGN OF δ₂ IS A COORDINATE, AND IT IS THE FIRST ONE THE GROUND STATE CANNOT SUPPLY.** *Seaton requires δ₂ < 0 for a polarisation series, so a positive δ₂ says the channel is not what the formula describes. Across 274 channels: **s 76% positive, p 74%, d 37%, f 6%, g 7%, h 9%**.* **The sign partitions the compendium into two populations with different physics and different error scales — median raw spread 0.0159 against 0.0029, median fit residual 0.0058 against 0.0003, U-test p < 10⁻⁵.**

### 1158

**And it names the transition zone exactly.** *np is 66% penetrating, **nd is 35%** and nf 9%.* **ℓ = 2 is the only orbital where the two populations sit together in comparable number**, and every step measured there has been averaging two physics — *which is why five separate corrections to the ℓ step failed and why the walk could never reach nd.*

### 1159

**The MAGNITUDE of δ₂ is a sixth coordinate and it does a different job: it predicts the channel's own scatter at R² = 0.761.** *Against ℓ alone at 0.230 and the sign at 0.267 — and adding the sign to the magnitude adds **nothing**, 0.761 to 0.761.* **The sign says which physics; the magnitude says how well the channel is determined.**

### 1160

**Which makes |δ₂| a better gate than the spread the compendium currently uses.** *Every threshold — the joint-fit precondition, the two-member gate, the walk's halt at 2.5 — tests the raw spread, and register 1150 established the spread is **48% δ₂ by construction**.* **A gate on |δ₂| is not circular: the spread is an outcome, δ₂ is a fitted parameter of the channel's own curve.**

### 1161

**The three quantities do NOT separate, and that is the structural finding rather than a shortfall.** *δ₀ against |δ₂| gives r² = 0.270; the sign against δ₀ gives 0.240.* **They are three views of one coupled system — nucleus, core, Rydberg electron — and no two of them are orthogonal.** *Which is the reason δ₂ resisted every occupancy-derived predictor in register 1156: an occupancy count is a ONE-BODY statement about the core, and δ₂ is a TWO-BODY statement about core and electron together.*

### 1162

**So the index has coordinates of two kinds and the survey's premise is qualified.** *Z, charge, ℓ and multiplicity are DERIVED — the ground state gives all four for all 118 elements, 101,328 cells. The regime and the magnitude class are MEASURED, and nothing derives them.* **A cell's regime can be guessed at 91% for ℓ ≥ 3 and 75% for ℓ ≤ 1, and NOT AT ALL at ℓ = 2** — *which is the row that has resisted every method tried today.*

### 1163

**The index is finished, and it carries a regime assignment for every cell.

Mechanism stated: where the NEUTRAL has an open d^2 (Hf Th Rf) or an f^n-d coupling (Gd Cm Pa U Ce), removing the d loses that term energy while removing
the s keeps it -> D_d deepens, gap = D_d - D_s DECREASES (toward s-first) on exactly those rows; on d^1 s^2 rows (Sc Y La Lu Ac) the neutral is a doublet
and only the s-removed ion (d^1 s^1 triplet) gains a small term -> gap INCREASES slightly (toward d-first).

PT-2  Gd: gap moves to <= -0.010 (s-first HELD; f7-d exchange lost on d removal). Cm: stays d-first (gap 0.046 - 0.02..0.03 > 0).
PT-3  Hf is the row at risk: gap +0.028 - (0.02..0.035) -> within +-0.01 of zero; Rf stays d-first (0.091 - 0.03). Pa/U: gap decreases by <= 0.02, stay d-first.

      form question, not by terms.
PT-5  Correlation stays as measured (class-flat +0.014); its interaction with terms is not predicted (comparison decides after PT-1..4).
Design decisions to make BEFORE the run: (i) which ion terms are the ground terms (from the record's term tables, RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED, not measured energies);

chat_messages.text:
Plainly, then.

**What the run does.** An atom's electrons can arrange themselves in several ways within the same shell occupancy, and some arrangements sit lower in energy than the shell-average. That extra lowering is the *term energy*. When you remove a d electron you may destroy that lowering; when you remove an s electron you keep it. So the term energy shifts the d-removal and s-removal costs by *different* amounts — and it shifts them by different amounts on *different rows*. That is why it's the only candidate left for the Th/Ac split: every other term measured so far moved all rows equally.

**The three decisions.**

**(i) Where the ion's arrangement comes from.** To compute the shift I need to know which arrangement each ion actually settles into. Two ways: read the published term symbol from the record (e.g. "Th⁺ ground term is ⁴F"), or compute the lowest arrangement myself from the Slater–Condon machinery. Reading it is safe and standard but takes a label from the record; computing it keeps the chain closed but risks landing on the wrong arrangement and quietly poisoning the row. The label carries no energy number either way.

**(ii) Whether the orbitals move.** The term energy is built from integrals over orbitals. I can use the average-configuration orbitals, frozen — same for every term — or let each arrangement relax its own orbitals. Frozen gives a clean term number. Relaxed gives a more physical number but mixes relaxation back in, and relaxation is already a separate object (B2). Frozen is what the prediction file assumed.

**(iii) Whether spin–orbit goes in now.** Th and Ac are heavy; spin–orbit is not small there. Left out, the number is a pure term energy and the mechanisms stay separated. Put in, the number is closer to the real atom but two mechanisms arrive in one figure and neither can be attributed alone.

The stake in all three is the same: each choice either keeps a mechanism separable or fuses two. My reading is (i) record labels, (ii) frozen, (iii) no spin-orbit — that's what the filed prediction was written against, and PT-1..5 only mean something if the run matches the design they were written for.

Studied. The rows do determine all three — here is what they say.

**The 13 rows fall into three classes by configuration alone**

| class | rows | neutral | d-removed ion | arrangement freedom |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Sc Y La Lu **Ac** | d¹s² | **closed shell** | none — term ≡ 0 on the d side |
| B | Hf **Th** Rf | d²s² | d¹ | d² has real freedom (³F ¹D ³P ¹G ¹S) |
| C | Ce Gd Pa U Cm | fⁿd¹s² | fⁿ | f¹, f⁷ forced; f² f³ free |

**Th and Ac are in different classes.** Th's neutral carries an open d²; Ac's does not, and Ac's d-removed ion has no open shell at all, so its term is exactly zero by configuration. The one term that is present at Th and structurally absent at Ac is the only row-differential object on the pair — and it arrives from the configurations, not from a fit. That is what makes the residual reachable.

**(i) settled by class A and the forced shells.** Sc, Y, La, Lu, Ac have zero arrangement freedom; so do Ce (f¹), Gd and Cm (f⁷ half-filled, forced), and every d¹ ion. On those rows the record's label cannot be anything else. So the machinery computes them, and the record label sits alongside as a comparison column. If the computed arrangement reproduces the record where the record is forced, the machinery is validated and can be used on Hf/Th/Rf and Pa/U where freedom exists. The label is never an input — recalled-not-entered holds, and the ambiguous rows get a measured answer rather than a chosen one.

**(ii) settled by the zero rows and a flatness test.** On the five class-A rows the d-side term is identically zero, so frozen and relaxed must agree exactly there — any difference is machinery error, and the rows report it. On the rows where a term exists, frozen-minus-relaxed is measured across all 13 and tested for class-flatness with the same instrument that closed the exchange seam. Flat means it is a seam, not row-differential, and frozen is then safe for the Th/Ac question. The test decides; neither of us does.

**(iii) cannot be assumed away, and the rows say why.** Spin-orbit is itself row-differential — it grows with Z, and Th/Ac sit at the heavy end. Left out by fiat, it stays a live alternative explanation for exactly the pair we're trying to close. So: LS terms computed on all 13, ζ computed per row as a separate column, and the comparison asks whether the residual tracks the **term structure** (present at Th, absent at Ac) or tracks **Z** (Ac 89, Th 90 — nearly identical, so Z predicts almost no split). """nlwalk_hf.py -- s37 Stage 2 of the n+l walk: SR HF (hfc2, no corr) DSCF removals on the frontier of the neutral. lwalk_hf.py generalised:
entrant g derived from ground.expand; removals = g and every OCCUPIED frontier partner (channels rule of nlwalk.py: (N,0)(N,1)(N-1,2)(N-2,3)).
D_rel(x) = E_neu - E(neu minus x) (negative = bound). Shallowest removal = walk's first-ionised subshell (comparison column only).
usage: python3 nlwalk_hf.py Z ...  appends nlwalk_hf.jsonl (key Z,tag). No constant; no measured input."""
import sys,os,json,time
os.environ.setdefault("SIC_NOCLAMP","1"); os.environ.setdefault("SUBCELL","1")
import hfc2 as H; from t7c_kernel import C0; from t5_scf import ground_occ,minus; import ground as G
H.CORR=False
def entrant(Z):
    a={(n,l):k for n,l,k in G.expand(Z)}; b={(n,l):k for n,l,k in G.expand(Z-1)}
    up=[nl for nl in a if a[nl]-b.get(nl,0)>1e-9]; assert len(up)==1,(Z,up); return up[0]
def channels(Z):
    N=max(n for n,l,k in G.expand(Z)); ch=[(N,0),(N,1),(N-1,2)]
    if N>=6: ch.append((N-2,3))
    return ch
def tagof(c): return f"{c[0]}{'spdf'[c[1]]}"
OUT='nlwalk_hf.jsonl'; done={(d['Z'],d['tag']) for d in map(json.loads,open(OUT))} if os.path.exists(OUT) else set()
MAXIT=int(os.environ.get("HFMAXIT","100"))
for Z in map(int,sys.argv[1:]):
    g=entrant(Z); occ0=ground_occ(Z); od={(n,l):k for n,l,k in occ0}
    rem=[g]+[c for c in channels(Z) if c!=g and c[1]!=1 and od.get(c,0)>1e-9]
    todo=[c for c in rem if (Z,tagof(c)) not in done]
    for c in rem:
        if (Z,tagof(c)) in done: print("SKIP",Z,tagof(c))
    if not todo: continue
    t0=time.time(); h0=H.HFC(Z,occ0,c=C0); E0,_,it0,eps0=h0.run2()
    for c in todo:
        t1=time.time(); hs=H.HFC(Z,minus(occ0,c[0],c[1],1.0),c=C0); Es,_,its,_=hs.run2()

               it=[it0,its],conv=bool(its<MAXIT),sec=int(time.time()-t1))
        open(OUT,'a').write(json.dumps(o)+'\n'); print(o,flush=True)

Studied. The rows do determine all three — here is what they say.

**The 13 rows fall into three classes by configuration alone**

| class | rows | neutral | d-removed ion | arrangement freedom |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Sc Y La Lu **Ac** | d¹s² | **closed shell** | none — term ≡ 0 on the d side |
| B | Hf **Th** Rf | d²s² | d¹ | d² has real freedom (³F ¹D ³P ¹G ¹S) |
| C | Ce Gd Pa U Cm | fⁿd¹s² | fⁿ | f¹, f⁷ forced; f² f³ free |

**Th and Ac are in different classes.** Th's neutral carries an open d²; Ac's does not, and Ac's d-removed ion has no open shell at all, so its term is exactly zero by configuration. The one term that is present at Th and structurally absent at Ac is the only row-differential object on the pair — and it arrives from the configurations, not from a fit. That is what makes the residual reachable.

**(i) settled by class A and the forced shells.** Sc, Y, La, Lu, Ac have zero arrangement freedom; so do Ce (f¹), Gd and Cm (f⁷ half-filled, forced), and every d¹ ion. On those rows the record's label cannot be anything else. So the machinery computes them, and the record label sits alongside as a comparison column. If the computed arrangement reproduces the record where the record is forced, the machinery is validated and can be used on Hf/Th/Rf and Pa/U where freedom exists. The label is never an input — recalled-not-entered holds, and the ambiguous rows get a measured answer rather than a chosen one.

**(ii) settled by the zero rows and a flatness test.** On the five class-A rows the d-side term is identically zero, so frozen and relaxed must agree exactly there — any difference is machinery error, and the rows report it. On the rows where a term exists, frozen-minus-relaxed is measured across all 13 and tested for class-flatness with the same instrument that closed the exchange seam. Flat means it is a seam, not row-differential, and frozen is then safe for the Th/Ac question. The test decides; neither of us does.

"""nlterm.py -- s38 item 1: term/multiplet energies on the WALK'S FIELD (hfc2, SR HF, no corr), both members of the d/s pair.
Design filed in PREDICTION-TERMS-VALIDATION-SESSION-38.md BEFORE this file existed.
(i)  the lowest term is COMPUTED by the Slater diagonal-sum rule over the open shell's determinants -- not asserted by Hund's rules.
     hund_det (max S then max L) is carried as a comparison column; the record's label is RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED, compared, never input.
(ii) FROZEN average-of-configuration orbitals of each state's own hfc2 SCF (the nlwalk_hf field). No per-term relaxation here.
(iii) LS only; no SO (zeta is a separate column, t7c_so).
sign convention: nlwalk's D_rel(x) = E_neu - E_ion(x)  (negative = bound). With terms E_tot = E_avg + dE_term (dE_term <= 0),

input.file_text:
# FINDING-TERMS (s38, item 1) — LS term/multiplet energies on the walk's field, 13 d/s rows (nlterm.py/.jsonl; TABLE-TERMS-SESSION-38).
Design filed BEFORE the run in PREDICTION-TERMS-VALIDATION-SESSION-38.md; that file's decisions (i)(ii)(iii) were DETERMINED BY THE ROWS
(M's ruling, s38), not chosen. No constant beyond c. Record first-ionised subshells and record ground-term labels RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED, comparison only.

## 1 · Machinery validated before any result was read
Gate PT0 (hfterm, inherited): determinant average == Slater average on d^2, f^2, d^3 and d^1s^1, |diff| <= 2.2e-16.
Gate PT8 (NEW, s38): the Slater DIAGONAL-SUM rule over all determinants of l^N — sum over determinants == sum over terms weighted (2S+1)(2L+1)
to 0..2.8e-17, determinant mean == E_avg to 1.7e-18, and the LOWEST term COMPUTED: d^2 -> 3F, f^2 -> 3H, f^3 -> 4I, f^7 -> 8S.
These are the record's Hund ground terms, reproduced by computation, and they agree with the hund_det (max S then max L) column on every row.
PV-1 HELD. Decision (i) is therefore settled BY MEASUREMENT: the arrangement is computed; the record label is a comparison column that agreed.
PV-2 HELD exactly: on class A (Sc Y La Lu Ac) the d-removed ion is closed-shell and its term energy is 0.00000 identically.
Field check: D_d and D_s reproduce nlwalk_hf to 5 dp on every row (Sc -0.26664/-0.20292 vs -0.2666/-0.2029; Lu -0.15979/-0.21137). The term column
sits on the WALK'S OWN FIELD, not a neighbouring one.

## 2 · THE STRUCTURAL RESULT: the neutral's term cancels out of the gap
gap = D_d - D_s, and with terms D_x(term) = D_x(avg) + dE(neu) - dE(ion_x). Therefore
        gap_term - gap_avg = dE_s - dE_d
and dE(neutral) DROPS OUT IDENTICALLY. The Hund-I term of the neutral's open d^2/f^n — the object PREDICTION-TERMS (s37) named as the mechanism —
cannot differentiate the pair at all. What differentiates is the TERM ENERGY OF THE TWO IONS, and specifically the s-removed ion, which retains the
whole open d (or f) shell AND gains an unpaired s to couple to it, while the d-removed ion has one electron fewer and often closes the shell outright.
Hence the shift is NEGATIVE ON ALL 13 ROWS (every row is pushed toward s-first) with size set by the ion's open-shell structure:
    class A (d^1 s^2, ion closed)   shift -0.0052 .. -0.0098   mean -0.0077
    class B (d^2 s^2, ion d^1)      shift -0.0387 .. -0.0480   mean -0.0438
    class C (f^n d^1 s^2, ion f^n)  shift -0.0189 .. -0.0504   mean -0.0389
This is the mechanism restated correctly by the run. The s37 statement ("removing the d loses that term energy -> D_d deepens") is not wrong about D_d —
D_d does deepen by dE(neu) — but D_s deepens by the SAME amount, so only the ion difference survives.

## 3 · The row-differential exists, and it is the first one measured on the pair
PV-7 HELD. The term correction is NOT class-flat: range 0.0052 to 0.0504, a factor of ten across rows, against every previously measured object
(exchange seam +0.034 +- 0.007 class-flat; S-correlation +0.014 class-flat). Th and Ac — adjacent in Z, split by class — are separated by
    Th shift -0.0387   Ac shift -0.0091   ->  row-differential 0.0296 Ha,
against the 0.016 Ha residual to be explained. The residual is REACHABLE by this mechanism and by no other object measured so far.
Th itself is resolved: gap +0.0083 (d-first, WRONG against the record) -> -0.0304 (s-first, RIGHT). PT-1 HELD. Ac stays d-first (+0.0240 -> +0.0149).
The one row HF got wrong is now right, and it is right for a stated structural reason: Th's ion keeps an open d, Ac's ion does not.

## 4 · AND THE CORRECTION AS APPLIED MAKES THE WALK WORSE, SO THE COMPARISON DECIDES AGAINST IT
SCORE: HF (no terms) 12/13. HF + LS terms 9/13. Fixed: Th. Broken: Hf (+0.0279 -> -0.0168), Pa (+0.0241 -> -0.0198), U (+0.0267 -> -0.0237),
Cm (+0.0463 -> -0.0009, a tie at the boundary). PV-6 FAILED (predicted >= 12/13 within +-0.010 of zero).
Per "comparison decides", LS terms in this form are NOT adopted into the walk field. Residue is not closure: the object is registered as MEASURED,
ROW-DIFFERENTIAL and REJECTED-AS-APPLIED, not carried as an improvement.
THE FAILURES ARE NOT SCATTERED. All four are the rows where LS coupling is least valid — Hf (5d), Pa U Cm (5f actinides). The LS term energy is an
UPPER BOUND on the real term splitting: spin-orbit mixes the LS terms and quenches the splitting, and it does so hardest exactly on 5f/6d.
Decision (iii)'s reason is now a measurement rather than a caution: SO cannot be left out, because the rows it would change are precisely the rows that broke.

## 5 · Failed predictions (logged, not suppressed) and what they cost
PV-4 (class A direction) FAILED. Predicted the gap to INCREASE toward d-first on d^1 s^2 rows; measured DECREASE on all five (-0.005..-0.010).
     Reason: the neutral term cancels (§2); the s-removed ion's d^1 s^1 triplet makes the s removal CHEAPER, pushing toward s-first. Direction of the
     class-A conclusion survives (Ac stays d-first) but the stated mechanism did not.
PV-6 FAILED (9/13, not >=12/13). PT-3 FAILED at Hf (predicted within +-0.010 of zero; measured -0.0168, class flipped). PT-2 FAILED at Cm (predicted
     stays d-first; measured -0.0009). PT-3's Pa/U clause FAILED (predicted decrease <= 0.02 and stay d-first; measured 0.044/0.050 and both flipped).
PT-1 HELD (Th <= -0.010, and Ac stays d-first). PV-1 PV-2 PV-7 HELD. PV-3 and PV-5 NOT TESTED this session — see open items.
Timing flags: none; every prediction above was filed before nlterm.py existed. Faults: F38.1 (rebuild, §H — .json data files omitted from the pack
layering loop; eps0a_table.json missing; caught at the OPEN gates, repaired, all 71 gates re-run from clean before any new work; no result read from the
faulted state).

## 6 · Open, in the order the finding leaves them
(a) SO / intermediate coupling as the companion to terms — now the leading candidate, and PV-5's separation test is unrun. zeta per row (t7c_so /
    t7c_3dhund machinery) against the four broken rows: if SO quenching restores Hf Pa U Cm while leaving Th fixed, the pair closes on terms+SO.
(b) PV-3 frozen-vs-relaxed (decision (ii)) is UNTESTED. The frozen convention was used; its bound is not yet measured. Class A gives the exact zero
    test (both must agree identically) and the flatness test is defined.
(c) correlation x terms (s37 item 2) unchanged, and now must be run on terms+SO rather than terms alone.

The rows determined all three decisions, and the machinery validated before any result was read — gate PT8 (new) closes the diagonal sum to 1e-17 and **computes** the lowest terms: d²→³F, f²→³H, f³→⁴I, f⁷→⁸S. **The structural result:** gap_term − gap_avg = dE_s − dE_d. **The neutral's term cancels out of the gap identically.** The mechanism s37 filed — the neutral's open d² Hund-I term — cannot differentiate the pair at all. What differentiates is the two *ions*: the s-removed ion keeps the whole open shell and gains an unpaired s to couple to it; the d-removed ion has one electron fewer and often closes outright. # PREDICTION-SO-SIGN (s38, item 1a) — WRITTEN BEFORE ANY ZETA IS COMPUTED THIS SESSION (R 1449).
Tests the candidate FINDING-TERMS §4 named as leading: that SO restores the four rows LS terms broke (Hf Pa U Cm) while leaving Th fixed.

## Mechanism, stated before the numbers
FINDING-TERMS §2 established gap_term - gap_avg = dE_s - dE_d: the NEUTRAL CANCELS. The same algebra holds for ANY additive state energy, so
        gap_SO - gap_LS = so(ion_s) - so(ion_d),
and SO also enters the gap ONLY through the two ions. Landé, first order, ground level of each ion:
    E_SO = (A/2)[J(J+1) - L(L+1) - S(S+1)],  A = +zeta/(2S) for a less-than-half-filled shell, A = -zeta/(2S) for more-than-half.
Class B (Hf Th Rf): d-removed ion d^1 2D_3/2 -> E = -1.5 zeta_d.  s-removed ion d^2 s^1 4F_3/2, A = zeta_d/3 -> E = -2.0 zeta_d.
    so(ion_s) - so(ion_d) = -0.5 zeta_d  <  0.
Class C (Pa U Cm): d-removed ion f^n (SO of the f shell alone). s-removed ion f^n d^1 s^1 — THE SAME f^n PLUS a d electron that the d-removed ion
    has lost. To first order the f^n part is common and cancels, leaving the extra d electron's SO: so(ion_s) - so(ion_d) ~ -1.5 zeta_d < 0.
Class A (Sc Y La Lu Ac): d-removed ion CLOSED (E_SO = 0); s-removed ion d^1 s^1 3D_1, A = zeta_d/2 -> E = -1.5 zeta_d. Difference -1.5 zeta_d < 0.

## PS-1  THE SIGN IS NEGATIVE ON EVERY CLASS. SO pushes every row FURTHER toward s-first, in the SAME direction as the LS term correction.
        Therefore SO CANNOT restore Hf, Pa, U, Cm. FINDING-TERMS §4's "SO quenches the LS term" is predicted WRONG IN SIGN and this file says so
        before the numbers are in. Quenching is the wrong picture: SO does not shrink the ground state's stabilisation below the configuration
        average, it ADDS to it — the average of configuration is invariant to SO, and the ground level lies below the LS ground term, not above it.
PS-2  Magnitude: with zeta_5d(Hf) ~ 0.006-0.010 and zeta_6d(Th) ~ 0.010-0.014 (bracketed by the banked La 5d 0.00308 and Lr 6d 0.01122, both COMPUTED
        in earlier sessions, RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED), the class-B SO gap shift is -0.5 zeta_d = -0.003 .. -0.007 Ha. Hf goes from -0.0168 to about
        -0.020 .. -0.024: FURTHER from its record, not nearer. Th goes from -0.0304 to -0.034 .. -0.037: still s-first, still RIGHT.
PS-3  Score prediction: HF + LS terms + SO <= 9/13, i.e. NO BETTER than terms alone, and Cm (-0.0009, a boundary tie) is predicted to move decisively
        s-first, so 9/13 is the ceiling and 9/13 the likely value.
PS-4  If instead the computed difference comes out POSITIVE on class B or C, PS-1 is falsified, SO is back as the companion, and the Landé assignment
        of the ion ground levels must be re-derived (the likely error would be the A-sign for a more-than-half-filled f shell at Cm).
PS-5  What this leaves: if PS-1 holds, the residual's companion is NOT SO. The next candidate is the F^k scale itself — HF F^k are known to exceed the
        real ones because correlation screens the multipole interaction, and the term correction scales LINEARLY in F^k. A uniform reduction factor
        would shrink class B (-0.044) and class C (-0.039) far more than class A (-0.008), which is the shape needed. That is s37 item 2
        (correlation x terms) and it is now the ruling candidate, not a queued one. NOT run here; stated so the design precedes the result.

## Held
No constant beyond c. First order Landé only; no diagonalisation in intermediate coupling (that is a later column, and PS-1's sign does not depend on it:
the ground level of each ion lies at or below its LS term in every coupling scheme, and the s-removed ion carries the extra d electron in all classes).

# FINDING-SO (s38, item 1a) — first-order Landé SO on the walk's pair, 13 rows (soz.py/.jsonl; TABLE-SO-SESSION-38).
Design filed in PREDICTION-SO-SIGN-SESSION-38.md BEFORE any zeta was computed this session. No constant beyond c; record first-ionised
subshells RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED, comparison only. zeta on the TS object (half hole in the channel), the s19 convention, inherited.

## 1 · Cross-check before the result was read
zeta_3d(Sc) = 0.00052 — IDENTICAL to the banked t7c_3dhund value from s25. The SO channel reproduces across thirteen sessions.
zeta_5d(Hf) = 0.00756 and zeta_6d(Th) = 0.00879 fall between the banked La 5d (0.00308) and Lr 6d (0.01122), as PS-2 bracketed.

## 2 · PS-1 HELD, AND IT KILLS THE CANDIDATE
The §2 algebra of FINDING-TERMS extends to SO: gap_SO - gap_LS = so(ion_s) - so(ion_d), THE NEUTRAL CANCELS AGAIN. Measured:
    so_gap NEGATIVE ON 13 OF 13 ROWS. Class A -0.0008..-0.0097 (-1.5 zeta_d), class B -0.0038..-0.0077 (-0.5 zeta_d), class C -0.0051..-0.0167.
SO therefore pushes EVERY row in the SAME direction as the LS term correction — further toward s-first — and cannot restore Hf, Pa, U, Cm.
SCORE: HF 12/13; HF + LS terms 9/13; HF + terms + SO 9/13. PS-3 HELD (9/13 was named as both ceiling and likely value).
FINDING-TERMS §4's speculation — "the LS term energy is an upper bound that SO quenches" — IS WRONG IN SIGN, and PREDICTION-SO-SIGN said so
before the numbers, with the reason: the average of configuration is invariant to SO, and the ground level lies BELOW its LS term in every
coupling scheme, so SO ADDS stabilisation rather than removing it. Quenching was the wrong picture of intermediate coupling.
The failures are unchanged in identity (Hf Pa U Cm) and worse in size: Cm moves from a -0.0009 boundary tie to -0.0176, decisively wrong.

## 3 · What survives, and one row now marginal
Th stays fixed and correct: -0.0348 (record s-first). Ac stays d-first at +0.0052 — but that is down from +0.0240 in HF, and it is now the
SMALLEST correct margin in the table. Registered as a marginal row: any further negative-going term of ~0.005 Ha flips it, so Ac is the next
row at risk and must be checked against every subsequent correction, not only the four that are already wrong.
The Th/Ac pair remains separated and remains correct under terms+SO, which is more than HF alone achieved (HF had Th wrong).

## 4 · Failed predictions (logged)
PS-2 magnitude, partial miss: zeta_6d(Th) predicted 0.010-0.014, measured 0.00879 — below the bracket. The Hf clause held (-0.00378 inside
-0.003..-0.007) and the class-B gap-shift clause held. PS-1, PS-3 HELD. PS-4 not triggered (no positive sign appeared, so the Landé A-sign
